newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline trims losses on US appetite, Med tight.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline trims losses on US appetite, Med tight.

text.p: European gasoline prices ended steady to slightly lower on Monday as healthy U.S. demand for both NWE and Med material cushioned an early selloff tied to Friday's tumble in crude, traders said.

No cargoes were heard fixed for the U.S. on Monday but they said the arbitrage was still open from the Med and NWE for the States, for large vessels of 60,000 tonnes. A slight rebound in NYMEX gasoline futures on Monday stoked trans-Atlantic interest, traders said.
Tight supplies, particularly for regular unleaded in NWE and low octane in the eastern Mediterranean, also supported prices, extending last week's trend.

"Overall (in NWE), I would say it's balanced, short in regular and long in Eurograde and 98 (unleaded)," a London trader said, adding the barge market was more amply supplied than cargoes. "The Med is really tight."
Eurograde barges were last heard at $217/$219 fob ARA, up $1 from its day's low but $2 below Friday. Regular unleaded held $5 below Eurograde at $212/$214.
A 30,000 tonne cargo out of the U.K. was still heard on offer into NWE for loading Feb 15-20, but this could not be confirmed and no fixed price was heard, traders said.
A 60,000 tonne cargo was confirmed sold late last week out of the U.K. for the U.S. for mid-February.
NWE premium unleaded cargoes were notionally unchanged at $214/$216 fob and $222/$224 cif
"We are still receiving fairly good demand for gasoline, mainly unleaded and for U.S. destinations...and low octane for the eastern Med," said one Italian trader.
The trader cited high freight rates, tight supplies of low octane, and healthy U.S. demand for buoying local prices.
